name: Regent Beijing
positioning: Beijing hotel directly above Dengshikou subway station, with Cantonese, Italian and steakhouse restaurants and a 17th-floor club lounge
best_for: Travelers who want to get around Beijing by subway from the hotel
Food-focused travelers who want several restaurants on site

facts.text: Transfers to and from Beijing Capital International Airport, a 50-minute journey, can be arranged on request.
Serenity Spa offers a menu of holistic treatments.
The hotel has an indoor pool.
The hotel has 1,600 square metres of flexible event space.
Weddings include a chauffeur-driven Rolls Royce for the duration of the stay.
Daccapo serves upscale Italian fare including handmade pastas, risotto and seafood.
Morton's of Chicago steakhouse has private dining suites.
Jinbao 99 is the all-day dining restaurant, with open kitchens and Asian and international dishes.
Higher floors offer better skyline views and occasional glimpses toward the Forbidden City.
Room decor includes walnut wood furniture, cream and beige tones, lacquer accents and the occasional Chinese-inspired art piece.
The hotel includes elevators, wheelchair access to common areas and accessible public facilities.

highlights.text: Lei Garden, from the Hong Kong-based Cantonese restaurant group known for helping popularize XO sauce, is the hotel's biggest dining draw.
The hotel is located above Dengshikou Station on Subway Line 5.
Guests can have Forbidden City Afternoon Tea in the Lobby Lounge and Bar.
The Regent Club lounge is on the 17th floor.
Even standard rooms come with separate soaking tubs and rain showers.

considerations.text: Tiananmen Square is less than a mile away and the Forbidden City is roughly 1.5 miles from the hotel.
WhataHotel notes the hotel is in a busy commercial district with heavy foot traffic.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing reflecting the high-end positioning.

sources.title: Conde Nast Traveler: Regent Beijing review
